objective: Proof and verification, for any near side. A crossing knot one of whose excluded patterns is separated by a single port (the near part forces the port one way, the far part the other) is the elimination through that port of two circuits, its near part with the port and its far part with the port. Check on plane and non-planar splices.
status: Proved by PLANAR-THEOREM-20261102-001B-P001: a crossing knot with an excluded pattern separated by a single port y is a 2-sum, for any near side and removal. y lies outside the knot, its near part plus y and far part plus y are circuits, and eliminating y gives the knot; if y is tied to a point of the knot, that point is alone on its side and the knot is tie-equivalent to a one-sided circuit. Uses only the join lemma, complement symmetry and minimality; checked on 33,556 separated crossing knots (plane and non-planar near sides)
title: Knots separated by one port are 2-sums
